tools.name: SendFeedback
tools.description:
Use this tool to draft feedback about Claude Code when you hit a high-signal moment. That includes both PRODUCT issues and MODEL-BEHAVIOR issues:
- a reproducible tool or product failure was just resolved or abandoned
- the user clearly expressed frustration with Claude Code or with how you handled the task
- you hit a missing capability that blocked a reasonable request
- you notice, or the user points out, that your own behavior in this session went wrong, for example: you gave a confident answer then had to retract it; you stopped short and handed work back when you could have finished; you declined or disputed a reasonable request; you spawned more subagents than the task warranted; your tone was off; you asked more clarifying questions than needed; you expanded scope beyond what was asked

The draft is QUEUED LOCALLY. It is never sent without the user's explicit approval, and calling this tool renders no UI and does not interrupt the conversation, so never announce it or ask the user about it mid-task.

Write `details` as short labeled bullets in this exact order, one to three lines each, no narrative paragraphs:
- **What happened:** the observed behavior vs. what was expected, with exact error text if short. Facts only.
- **What the user said:** the user's own words that prompted this, quoted. If nothing did, write "User didn't comment; observed by the model." Never paraphrase sentiment into a stronger claim.
- **Repro:** the minimal steps or shape that reproduces it.
- **Evidence:** identifiers a reader can chase, such as request IDs, timestamps, file paths, versions. Omit the bullet if there are none.

Constraints:
- Never fabricate or exaggerate user sentiment; report only what actually happened.
- Everything in the draft must be sourced from the user or the session, never inferred: leave unknown fields blank rather than guess, and add a final **Cause:** bullet only for a root cause you verified in-session.
- Use `area` to name the part of Claude Code the feedback is about (a feature, command, or workflow, e.g. "hooks config", "/help", "file editing") when there is a clear one; leave it blank otherwise.
- Use `failure_mode` ONLY when the report is about model behavior (how Claude responded), not a product bug. Pick the single closest value, or `other` when it is a model-behavior issue that fits no listed value; omit the field only when the report is a product/tool bug with no model-behavior component.
- Use `task_category` to name what kind of task the session was doing, or `other` when it is a clear task that fits no listed value. Omit only if genuinely unclear.
- Do not include secrets or credentials. Refer to people by role ("a teammate", "the PR reviewer"), never by name, email address, or chat/user ID. This applies inside quoted user words too: replace a name or handle with a bracketed role (e.g. "[a teammate]") and keep the rest verbatim. Do not include customer-facing channel or DM IDs, or excerpts of customer content. Session, request, and run IDs, timestamps, repo/PR numbers, and file paths (written relative to the working directory, or ~-prefixed, not absolute paths under the user's home) remain the right evidence.
- If the issue looks like a security vulnerability: describe the class of problem, never a working exploit or step-by-step extraction path.
- Draft only at the natural moments listed above, and at most one draft per distinct issue; never re-draft the same issue in a session.

tools.name: Skill
tools.description:
Invoke a skill.

A skill is a packaged set of instructions the user or project has set up for a particular kind of task (deploy steps, a review checklist, a repo-specific workflow). Available skills appear in a system-reminder listing with one-line descriptions. When the task at hand is one a listed skill covers, call this tool first — the skill's instructions load into the turn for you to follow in place of your default approach; some skills instead run in a subagent and return the finished result. A skill that runs in the background returns only the agent's name — its result arrives later as a task notification, so don't wait on it or invoke it again in the meantime. Users may also ask for one by name (`/<name>`, or "slash command"); that's a request to invoke it.

- `skill`: exact name from the listing, no leading slash. Plugin skills use `plugin:skill`. Directory-scoped skills are listed with a path prefix (`apps/web:deploy`); when both scoped and unscoped variants of a name exist, pick the one whose directory contains the files you're working on (most specific wins; unscoped otherwise).
- `args`: optional arguments to pass through.

Only names from the listing (or that the user typed explicitly) are valid. Built-in CLI commands (`/help`, `/clear`, …) aren't skills. If a `<command-name>` block is already present this turn, the skill is loaded — follow it directly rather than calling again.

tools.name: ToolSearch
tools.description:
Fetches full schema definitions for deferred tools so they can be called.

Deferred tools appear by name in <system-reminder> messages. Until fetched, only the name is known — there is no parameter schema, so the tool cannot be invoked. This tool takes a query, matches it against the deferred tool list, and returns the matched tools' complete JSONSchema definitions inside a <functions> block. Once a tool's schema appears in that result, it is callable exactly like any tool defined at the top of the prompt.

Result format: each matched tool appears as one <function>{"description": "...", "name": "...", "parameters": {...}}</function> line inside the <functions> block — the same encoding as the tool list at the top of this prompt.

Query forms:
- "select:Read,Edit,Grep" — fetch these exact tools by name

**Ingest**

**Seller**

- A sale creates an onboarding case. "Not Connected" or "Voicemail" sends a WhatsApp nudge.

**Onboarding**
- Cases are auto-assigned via the roster, and a backlog rebalance runs daily at 8:30 AM IST.

- Once ads have run, the merchant moves to CSM.

**CSM**
- Merchant queues: ending, ended, cancelled, lapsed and closed.
- CSMs call about Top-up, Upgrade, Renew or Refund.
- WhatsApp templates T1–T5 go out after the daily sync.

- Each sent template is logged in `wa_messages`.
- When the merchant clicks `/cb/token`, it lands in the "Req Call Back" pane, which feeds back into the Seller, Onboarding and CSM workspaces.

**Database**
- Neon Postgres holds `calls`, `onboarding_cases`, the `csm_*` tables, `merchant_information`, `leadgen_leads`, `ct_payment_events` and `wa_messages`.

**Analytics**
- Seller/Onboarding analytics, date-effective incentive plans, and an Excel payout workbook.

# Pi Commerce Call Center Disposition — Project Explanation

## What it is

An internal web portal for the Pi Commerce calling teams. It replaced a Google Sheet ("Disposition Sheet - Sellers") where agents logged every call to a merchant by hand.

Now an agent logs in, looks up a merchant by **Cust ID** (or phone), sees that merchant's full call history, and logs the outcome of the new call (the **disposition**). Everything is stored in a Neon Postgres database, and on top of that the portal runs work queues, WhatsApp follow-ups, analytics and incentive payouts.

## The three teams (workspaces)

The portal has three workspaces. What a person can open depends on their access (`lib/workspace-access.ts`, `lib/teams.ts`).

| Workspace | Team | Job | Main screen |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Seller** | Sales (BDE / SBDE / TL) | Sell subscriptions to merchants | `app/page.tsx` → `components/AgentConsole.tsx` |
| **Onboarding** | Onboarding | Get a merchant who just paid to their first live ad | `app/onboarding` → `components/OnboardingConsole.tsx` |
| **CSM** | Customer Success | Merchants whose ads have run: renewals, top-ups, upgrades | `app/csm` → `components/CsmConsole.tsx` |

The customer moves through them in order: **Seller sells → Onboarding gets the ad live → CSM keeps the merchant paying.**

## Core idea: dispositions

Each call is logged with a three-level outcome:

- **L0**: the broad result, e.g. Interested, Not Connected, Callback, Not Interested, Plan Upgraded
- **L1**: a sub-reason
- **L2**: the specific detail

The tree lives in database tables (`disposition_nodes`, `onboarding_disposition_nodes`), so admins can change it without a code deploy.

Data-safety rules:

- **Every call creates a new row.** Old calls are never edited, and same-day calls are never merged.
- **The label text is copied onto the call when it's saved.** Renaming a disposition later doesn't rewrite history.
- **Historical calls from the old Google Sheet are kept exactly as they were** (old status and remark text). They are never forced into L0/L1/L2.

## Main features

### Seller workspace
- Search a customer, see their timeline, log a call.

content.text:
Yes. Nothing in the code ties it to Vercel.

**Why it moves cleanly**
- It's a plain Next.js 15 app: `next build` then `next start`. There are no `@vercel/*` packages, no edge runtime and no Vercel crons.
- The scheduled jobs are Apps Script timers that call your URLs, so only those URLs change.
- `after()` (in `api/calls`, `onboarding/events`, `csm-sync`, `csm/merchants`) works under `next start`. It actually behaves better on a long-running server.
- `maxDuration` is ignored on EC2, and there's no timeout to worry about.
- The database stays on Neon. Put EC2 in **ap-south-1 (Mumbai)** so it sits next to the database.
- `go-api` already wants to be a long-running service, and EC2 suits that better than Vercel. Its 5-minute rebalance clock was designed for a server like this.

**What you'd have to handle yourself**
1. **HTTPS.** Run Caddy (automatic certificates) in front of Next.js on :3000 and go-api on :8080. The session cookie is `secure` in production, so login won't work without HTTPS.
2. **Process manager.** One systemd unit each for `next start` and `go-api`.
3. **Deploys.** You lose Vercel's push-to-deploy and preview URLs. Simplest replacement: a GitHub Action that SSHes in and runs `git pull && npm ci && npm run build && systemctl restart`.
4. **Env vars.** Move them into a `.env` file or SSM: `DATABASE_URL`, the secrets, `PI_WA_*`. Get the values with `vercel env pull`.
5. **Logs and monitoring.** Use journald or CloudWatch, plus an uptime check on `/healthz`.

**Things that will break if you just switch hosts**
- **WhatsApp callback links.** The `/cb/<token>` host isn't in the code, so it must be set in the WhatsApp template button on the platform side. Templates and messages already sent point at `pi-commerce-call-center-disposition.vercel.app`. Keep the Vercel deployment up and redirect `/cb/*` to the new host, or get the templates re-approved with the new domain.
- **Apps Script URL properties.** All of them need the new host: `scripts/*.gs` and `docs/google-sheets-merchant-sync.gs`.
- **CleverTap webhook URL.**
- **`NEXT_BASE_URL` in go-api.** It should become `http://localhost:3000` because both run on the same box.

**Recommended path:** one t3.small or t3.medium in Mumbai, Caddy, and the two systemd services. Cut over one script at a time as described in `go-api/README.md`. Keep Vercel running until all the callers have moved, and then keep the `/cb` redirect running indefinitely.

Do you want me to write the systemd units, the Caddyfile and the deploy Action? You'd need to tell me your domain name.

content.text:
## Moving to EC2

| Item | Today | After |
|---|---|---|
| **Next.js portal** (agent screens, `/api/calls`, onboarding/CSM APIs, analytics, incentives, `/cb/<token>`, `wa-run`) | Vercel | EC2, `next start` on :3000 |
| **go-api** (sync endpoints, CleverTap webhook, 8:30 AM rebalance) | Not deployed yet | EC2, Go binary on :8080 |
| **HTTPS + domain** | Vercel handles it | Caddy on EC2 (automatic certificates) |
| **Env vars / secrets** | Vercel dashboard | `.env` on EC2, or AWS SSM |
| **Deploys** | Git push → Vercel | GitHub Action → SSH → build → restart |

## Staying where they are

- **Neon Postgres.** Same `DATABASE_URL`, no data migration.
- **Apps Script timers.** Only their URL properties change.
- **CleverTap and the WhatsApp platform.** Only the URLs change.
- **The Vercel deployment.** Keep it as a fallback and to redirect old `/cb` links.

## How to move it

**Phase 1: Set up EC2 (no traffic yet)**
1. Launch an EC2 instance in **ap-south-1 (Mumbai)**, t3.small or t3.medium, Ubuntu. Open ports 80 and 443 only.
2. Install Node 22, Go and Caddy.
3. Clone the repo and copy the env vars over (`vercel env pull` gives you the values).
4. Build:
   - `npm ci && npm run build`
   - `cd go-api && go build -o go-api .`
5. Add systemd units for `next start` and `go-api`.
6. Point a domain (e.g. `portal.yourdomain.com`) at the instance's Elastic IP. Configure Caddy to send `/api/internal/*` and `/api/admin/merchant-sync` to :8080 and everything else to :3000.
7. Set `NEXT_BASE_URL=http://localhost:3000` for go-api.
8. Check that `/healthz` returns `ok`, that login works, and that you can log a test call.

**Phase 2: Move the machine callers, one at a time**

This is the order from `go-api/README.md`. After each step, check the next run in the Apps Script log.

1. Ad conversions sync

content.text:
Short answer: the auth code doesn't need to change. It runs fine on EC2. What changes is the setup around it.

## How auth works today

`lib/auth.ts` keeps sessions in the database:
- Login gives the browser a random token in the `pi_session` cookie and stores only its sha256 hash in the `sessions` table. Sessions last 7 days.
- Every API call goes through `currentAgent()` or `currentUserAccess()`, which looks up the session in the database.
- Machine endpoints check a shared secret header with `timingSafeEqual`.

None of this depends on Vercel. Sessions live in Neon, so they keep working on any host.

## Must do

1. **Serve over HTTPS.** The cookie is set with `secure: NODE_ENV === 'production'`, and `next start` sets production mode. Over plain HTTP, browsers drop the cookie and login silently fails. Caddy fixes this.
2. **Keep ports 3000 and 8080 private.** Bind them to `127.0.0.1` and open only 80 and 443 in the security group. If 8080 is reachable from outside, the sync secrets travel over plain HTTP and the TLS layer can be bypassed.
3. **Expect one re-login.** The cookie belongs to the vercel.app domain, so on the new domain every agent logs in once. No database change is needed.
4. **Shut the old portal.** Vercel and EC2 share the same database, so a session works on both. After cutover, the vercel.app copy is a second way in. Strip Vercel down to the `/cb` redirect or turn on Vercel Deployment Protection.
5. **Protect secrets on the box.** Use a `.env` file with `chmod 600` owned by the service user, or AWS SSM Parameter Store. Don't commit it and don't put it in user-data.

## Should do

6. **Throttle login.** `api/auth/login` has no rate limit or lockout today. Vercel's edge absorbed some abuse; a bare EC2 instance won't. Options:
   - a small in-memory counter per IP in the login route (works because there's one instance),
   - or AWS WAF with a rate rule if you put an ALB in front.
7. **Lock down server access.** Use AWS SSM Session Manager or SSH keys only, with no password SSH. Give the instance an IAM role with only the permissions it needs.
8. **Rotate the secrets** (`SUB_RAW_SYNC_SECRET`, `CT_WEBHOOK_SECRET`, `MERCHANT_SYNC_SECRET`). You'll be updating the Apps Script properties and the CleverTap webhook anyway, so rotation costs almost nothing.

## Unchanged

- The password hashing in `lib/password.ts`.
- The roles and workspace-access rules.
- The `sessions` table.
- The secret checks on the machine endpoints.

Do you want me to add the login rate limit now? It's about 15 lines in the login route.

I pulled the latest `main`, which brought in 12 new commits and `f9e389e` as HEAD. The only leftover local file is `explanation.md`.

`go-api/` and `app/api/internal/wa-run/` are no longer on disk. `git pull` doesn't delete untracked files, so they were removed some other way. Neither is in the repo. That fits your plan, but if you wanted to keep a copy, it's gone.

## Revised plan: one Next.js app on EC2, demo only

**What runs on EC2:** the Next.js portal, started with `next start` behind Caddy for HTTPS.

**What doesn't change:** Neon, Vercel, the Apps Script triggers, CleverTap and Voice AI. They all keep calling Vercel. For a demo, don't move any callers. Vercel keeps running production.

**Code changes:** none. The new code still has no Vercel-specific packages or settings.

## Steps

1. **Launch the instance.** EC2 in ap-south-1, t3.small, Ubuntu 24.04. Open ports 22 (your IP only), 80 and 443.
2. **Install:** Node 22, git and Caddy.
3. **Get the code:**
   ```sh
   git clone https://github.com/MRG15/Pi-Commerce-Call-Center-Disposition-.git app
   cd app && npm ci && npm run build
   ```
4. **Create `.env`** (`chmod 600`) with:
   - `DATABASE_URL`
   - `SUB_RAW_SYNC_SECRET`
   - `MERCHANT_SYNC_SECRET`
   - `CT_WEBHOOK_SECRET`
   - `VOICE_AI_CALLBACK_SECRET` (new in this code)
   - `PI_WA_API_KEY`, `PI_WA_FROM`, `PI_WA_URL`, `PI_WA_TEST_CUSTOMERS`

   `vercel env pull` gives you the values.
5. **Run it with systemd:** `next start -H 127.0.0.1 -p 3000`, restart on failure.
6. **Set up Caddy.** With a domain, Caddyfile is `demo.yourdomain.com { reverse_proxy 127.0.0.1:3000 }`. With no domain, see below.
7. **Check it:** log in and open each workspace.
8. **To update later:** `git pull && npm ci && npm run build && sudo systemctl restart pi-portal`.

## Two demo risks

- **Shared database.** If EC2 uses the production `DATABASE_URL`, every demo call is written to real data and can trigger real WhatsApp messages to merchants. Safer: create a **Neon branch** (a copy of production) for the demo, and leave `PI_WA_API_KEY` unset or point `PI_WA_TEST_CUSTOMERS` at test numbers.
- **No domain means no HTTPS, and then login fails** because of the secure cookie. Options:
  - a free subdomain such as `<ip>.sslip.io`, which Caddy can get a certificate for,
  - or set `NODE_ENV` differently for the demo. Not recommended.

The auth points from earlier still apply, apart from the ones that only mattered for the full cutover.

Should the demo use a Neon branch or production? And do you have a domain, or should I use sslip.io? Once I know, I'll write the systemd unit, the Caddyfile and a setup script.

## Cutover steps

**1. Build EC2 (no traffic yet)**

  - the `PI_WA_*` variables
- Set up a systemd service and Caddy, and point the domain at an Elastic IP.
- Check that login works and that each workspace loads.

**2. Move the machine callers, one at a time**

Running Vercel and EC2 in parallel is safe because the syncs take advisory locks. After each step, check the next run in its log.
1. Apps Script: ad conversions
2. Apps Script: merchant sync

**5. Shut Vercel**

**Rollback:** at any step, point the URL back to vercel.app. Nothing in the database changes.

content.text:
Here's the move broken into steps. Replace `portal.example.com` with your domain throughout.

## Phase 0: Prep (on your laptop, about 10 minutes)

**Step 1. Back up the env vars from Vercel.**
```sh
vercel env pull .env.production --environment=production
```
Keep this file private and don't commit it.

**Step 2. Pick the domain.** For example `portal.example.com`. You'll point it at EC2 in Step 9.

**Step 3. Generate new secrets.** You're changing every caller's URL anyway, so this is the cheap moment to rotate them.
```sh
openssl rand -hex 32   # run once each: SUB_RAW_SYNC_SECRET, MERCHANT_SYNC_SECRET, CT_WEBHOOK_SECRET, VOICE_AI_CALLBACK_SECRET
```

## Phase 1: Create the server (AWS console)

**Step 4. Launch the instance.**
- Region: **ap-south-1 (Mumbai)**
- Ubuntu 24.04, t3.small (t3.medium if the Excel exports feel slow), 20 GB disk
- Key pair: create one or reuse an existing one

**Step 5. Security group.**
- 22: your IP only
- 80: anywhere
- 443: anywhere
- Nothing else. Port 3000 stays private.

**Step 6. Elastic IP.** Allocate one and attach it to the instance, so the IP survives reboots.

## Phase 2: Set up the server (SSH in)

**Step 7. Install Node 22, git and Caddy.**
```sh
curl -fsSL https://deb.nodesource.com/setup_22.x | sudo -E bash -
sudo apt-get install -y nodejs git debian-keyring debian-archive-keyring apt-transport-https
curl -1sLf 'https://dl.cloudsmith.io/public/caddy/stable/gpg.key' | sudo gpg --dearmor -o /usr/share/keyrings/caddy-stable-archive-keyring.gpg
curl -1sLf 'https://dl.cloudsmith.io/public/caddy/stable/debian.deb.txt' | sudo tee /etc/apt/sources.list.d/caddy-stable.list
sudo apt-get update && sudo apt-get install -y caddy
```

**Step 8. Clone and build.** The repo is private, so add a GitHub deploy key first: `ssh-keygen -t ed25519`, then paste the `.pub` into GitHub → repo Settings → Deploy keys, read-only.
```sh
sudo mkdir -p /opt/pi-portal && sudo chown ubuntu /opt/pi-portal
git clone [redacted]:MRG15/Pi-Commerce-Call-Center-Disposition-.git /opt/pi-portal
cd /opt/pi-portal && npm ci && npm run build
```

**Step 9. Create the env file.** Paste the values from Step 1, with the new secrets from Step 3.
```sh
nano /opt/pi-portal/.env.production
chmod 600 /opt/pi-portal/.env.production
```
It needs:
- `DATABASE_URL`
- `SUB_RAW_SYNC_SECRET`
- `MERCHANT_SYNC_SECRET`
- `CT_WEBHOOK_SECRET`
- `VOICE_AI_CALLBACK_SECRET`
- `PI_WA_API_KEY`, `PI_WA_FROM`, `PI_WA_URL`
- `PI_WA_TEST_CUSTOMERS`, only if it's set on Vercel

`next start` reads `.env.production` automatically.

**Step 10. Create the systemd service** at `/etc/systemd/system/pi-portal.service`:
```ini
[Unit]
Description=Pi Commerce portal
After=network.target

[Service]
User=ubuntu
WorkingDirectory=/opt/pi-portal
Environment=NODE_ENV=production
ExecStart=/usr/bin/npx next start -H 127.0.0.1 -p 3000
Restart=always

[Install]
WantedBy=multi-user.target
```
```sh
sudo systemctl daemon-reload && sudo systemctl enable --now pi-portal
curl -I http://127.0.0.1:3000/login   # expect 200
```

**Step 11. Point DNS.** Add an A record for `portal.example.com` with the Elastic IP as the value. Wait until `dig portal.example.com` returns that IP.

**Step 12. Set up Caddy** in `/etc/caddy/Caddyfile`:
```
portal.example.com {
    reverse_proxy 127.0.0.1:3000
}
```
```sh
sudo systemctl reload caddy
```
Caddy gets the HTTPS certificate on its own.

**Step 13. Smoke test** at `https://portal.example.com`:
- Log in.
- Open the seller, onboarding and CSM workspaces.
- Search a Cust ID.
- Open analytics.
- Do **not** log a test call yet, because this is production data.

## Phase 3: Move the callers (one per step; Vercel keeps running)

After each step, wait for the caller's next run and check the log (Apps Script → Executions). If one fails, put the old URL back.

**Step 14.** Ad conversions: `scripts/ad-conversions-sync.gs` → Project Settings → Script Properties → change the URL host and the secret.

**Step 15.** Merchant sync: `docs/google-sheets-merchant-sync.gs`, same as Step 14.

**Step 16.** Lead gen: `scripts/leadgen-sync.gs`. It runs every 5 minutes, so you'll know quickly.

**Step 17.** Sub Raw: `scripts/sub-raw-onboarding-sync.gs`. It runs daily.

**Step 18.** CSM: `scripts/csm-sync.gs`. It runs daily, and the WhatsApp T1–T5 messages follow it.

**Step 19.** CleverTap: update the webhook URL and secret in the CleverTap dashboard.

**Step 20.** Voice AI: send their team the new URL and secret for `/api/internal/voice-ai-callback`.

**Step 21.** Update `VOICE_AI_CALLBACK_SECRET` and the other secrets on Vercel as well, so both servers accept the same callers during the overlap. Or skip this if you move each caller in one go.

## Phase 4: Move the people

**Step 22.** Send agents the new URL. Each person logs in once.

**Step 23.** Log one real call and check that it appears in the timeline.

## Phase 5: WhatsApp links

**Step 24.** On Vercel, redirect `/cb/:path*` to `https://portal.example.com/cb/:path*`, so links already sent keep working.

**Step 25.** Update the WhatsApp template button URL on the platform to the new domain. It may need re-approval; until then, the redirect covers it.

## Phase 6: Shut Vercel down (after 3–5 quiet days)

**Step 26.** Strip the Vercel project down to the `/cb` redirect only, or enable Deployment Protection. Either way, the old portal stops being a second entrance to the same database.

**Step 27.** Update the URLs in the comments of the two `.gs` scripts and in `docs/voice-ai-callback-api.md`. Commit.

## Phase 7: Day-2 setup

**Step 28.** Deploy script on EC2:
```sh
cd /opt/pi-portal && git pull && npm ci && npm run build && sudo systemctl restart pi-portal
```
Later you can wrap this in a GitHub Action that runs it over SSH on every push to `main`.

**Step 29.** Monitoring:
- an uptime check on `https://portal.example.com/login`
- `journalctl -u pi-portal -f` for logs, or the CloudWatch agent

**Step 30.** Add the login rate limit (a small code change in `app/api/auth/login/route.ts`).

## Downtime and rollback

**Downtime:** close to zero. The database never moves, Vercel and EC2 run side by side, and each switch is one URL change.

**Rollback at any step:** put the vercel.app URL back. No data is affected.

Once you give me the domain, I can commit Steps 10, 12 and 28 as files in `deploy/`, and do Step 30 now.

content.text:
Voice AI comes in at the **Onboarding** stage of the flow. It's a way into the Req Call Back pane.

## Where it sits in the flow

```
Seller sale → Onboarding case created
                  │
     ┌────────────┴────────────┐
     ▼                         ▼
Onboarder calls          Onboarding voice AI calls merchant
merchant                  (external system, not in this repo)
     │                         │
     │              Merchant stuck / asks for a human
     │                         │
     │              POST /api/internal/voice-ai-callback
     │                         ▼
     └──────────►  Req Call Back pane (onboarding), tagged "Voice AI"
                               │
                     Owning onboarder calls back
                     → logs disposition → request clears
```

- **Who calls it:** the voice AI team's bot, through its "transfer to a human" tool. Our side only receives the call.
- **What happens:** `app/api/internal/voice-ai-callback/route.ts` matches the merchant by Cust ID, or by phone if there's no Cust ID, to an onboarding case. It then adds a row to `wa_messages` with template `VOICE_AI_HANDOFF`. No WhatsApp message is sent.
- **If no merchant matches:** the request is still saved and shows to onboarding admins as "Voice AI · unmatched".
- **Repeat calls:** while a request is open, a new call updates it instead of adding a duplicate.
- **Auth:** the `x-voice-ai-secret` header must match `VOICE_AI_CALLBACK_SECRET`.

Your Mermaid diagram doesn't include this yet. It would be one more box pointing into `W3["Req Call Back pane"]` and on to `O2`.

## In the migration

It's **Step 20**: send the voice AI team the new URL and secret.

This was added recently (PR #89). If their bot isn't calling it in production yet, the simplest route is to **give them the EC2 URL from the start**, so they never integrate against vercel.app. Then Step 20 is just updating `docs/voice-ai-callback-api.md` before you send it.

Do you know whether they're already calling the vercel.app URL?

Understood. Here's the migration covering only what's in your diagram.

## What happens to each part of the diagram

| Diagram block | Moves to EC2? | What changes |
|---|---|---|
| **External sources**: Google Sheets, CleverTap | No | CleverTap's webhook URL changes to the new domain |
| **Automated ingest**: Apps Script → `merchant-sync`, `leadgen-sync`, `sub-raw-onboarding-sync`, `csm-sync`, `ct-payment` | The endpoints move; the Apps Script timers stay in Google | Each script's URL property changes to the new domain |
| **Auth**: `/login`, `pi_session`, `sessions` table | Yes | No code change. Needs HTTPS. Agents log in once on the new domain |
| **Seller workspace** | Yes | None |
| **Onboarding workspace**, including the 8:30 AM rebalance | Yes | None. The rebalance still runs off `leadgen-sync` |
| **CSM workspace** | Yes | None |
| **WhatsApp nudges**: send, `/cb/token`, Req Call Back | Yes | Old `/cb` links point at vercel.app, so you need a redirect plus a template URL update |
| **Neon Postgres** | No | Same `DATABASE_URL` |
| **Analytics & payouts** | Yes | None |

## Steps

**A. Build the server**
1. Launch EC2 in Mumbai (t3.small, Ubuntu). Open 80 and 443, and 22 for your IP only. Attach an Elastic IP.
2. Install Node 22, git and Caddy.
3. `git clone` the repo, then `npm ci && npm run build`.
4. Create `.env.production` with `DATABASE_URL`, `SUB_RAW_SYNC_SECRET`, `MERCHANT_SYNC_SECRET`, `CT_WEBHOOK_SECRET` and the `PI_WA_*` variables.
5. Set up a systemd service running `next start -H 127.0.0.1 -p 3000`.
6. Point the domain's DNS at the Elastic IP. Configure Caddy to reverse-proxy to :3000 (it handles HTTPS).
7. Test: log in and open the Seller, Onboarding, CSM and Analytics screens.

**B. Move the ingest, one at a time** (check each one's next run)
1. `merchant-sync`
2. `leadgen-sync`
3. `sub-raw-onboarding-sync`
4. `csm-sync`
5. CleverTap → `ct-payment`

**C. Move the agents**
1. Share the new URL. Everyone logs in once.

**D. WhatsApp**
1. On Vercel, redirect `/cb/*` to the new domain.
2. Update the template button URL.

**E. Shut Vercel**
1. Keep only the `/cb` redirect.

**Rollback at any step:** point the URL back to vercel.app. The database is untouched.

content.text:
## CleverTap auth

CleverTap does **not** authenticate through the URL. The secret travels in a **header**:

```
x-ct-webhook-[redacted]
```

This is checked at `app/api/internal/ct-payment/route.ts:84-85` with `timingSafeEqual`.

So, in the CleverTap webhook settings:
- **Change:** the URL host, from vercel.app to the new domain.
- **Keep:** the header exactly as it is, as long as EC2's `.env` has the same `CT_WEBHOOK_SECRET` value. Only change it if you rotate the secret.

All the Apps Script syncs work the same way: a header (`x-sub-raw-sync-secret`, `x-merchant-sync-secret`) and no secret in the URL. Only the host changes.

## Possible pain points on AWS

| # | Issue | Risk | Fix |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | **CleverTap needs valid HTTPS.** It won't call plain HTTP or a self-signed certificate | High | Use Caddy with a real domain. A bare IP won't work |
| 2 | **Security group.** CleverTap's and Google's IPs aren't fixed | High | Open 443 to `0.0.0.0/0`. The header secrets protect the endpoints |
| 3 | **Server timezone.** Vercel runs in UTC, and some code reads local time (`lib/source-parser.ts:74,98`, `sub-raw-onboarding-sync/route.ts:156`) | Medium | Leave Ubuntu on its UTC default. **Don't set it to IST**, or dates shift by one day |
| 4 | **Single server.** Vercel had no single machine to fail; one EC2 does | Medium | If EC2 is down, CleverTap events are missed, but the next day's Sub Raw sync still creates the case. No permanent loss, only a one-day delay. Add an uptime alert. |
| 5 | **Process crash or reboot** | Low | systemd `Restart=always` plus `enable` (already in the plan) |
| 6 | **Disk filling with logs** | Low | journald rotates by default. Use a 20 GB disk |
| 7 | **Database connections** | None | `lib/db.ts` caps the pool at 5. One long-running process uses fewer connections than Vercel did |
| 8 | **Timeouts and payload size** | None (better than before) | EC2 has no 300-second limit and no 4.5 MB body cap. Large sheet syncs are safer |
| 9 | **Header passthrough** | None | Caddy forwards custom headers unchanged |

**Bottom line:** for CleverTap you only change the URL; the header stays. The two that matter most are #1 (a real domain with HTTPS) and #3 (keep the server on UTC).
